question: Nils had 121 old postcards in a drawer, and postage on them is quoted in cents rather than in dollars. Damp had ruined 22 of them, so he threw those away. A copy shop reproduced every surviving postcard 3 times for an exhibition. Nils and his colleague Petra split all the reproductions equally into 3 bundles, and Nils took one bundle for his own display. Petra, whose drawer held far less, gave him 17 further cards for the same display. Each card in his display needed 2 stamps, twice what an ordinary letter takes. How many stamps did Nils need?

A hill farm had 110 fence posts stacked behind the barn, and a timber yard delivered 58 more before the rain came. The top field runs to 7 hectares. Every post in the stack needed 2 metal brackets to hold the wire. The farmer found 44 spare brackets in an old toolbox and counted them with the others. He then used 131 of the brackets on the gates along the lane. How many brackets did the farmer have left?

The flower festival opened the morning with 40 pots of lilies on the display bench. Before ten o'clock 11 pots were bought by early visitors. A grower arrived at noon with 72 fresh pots, which joined the bench. The marquee itself is 60 metres long. During the afternoon the stewards counted 3 stems standing in every pot, and each stem carried 6 open blooms. By evening the heat had wilted 991 of the blooms and they were snipped off. How many blooms were still on the bench at closing time?

Marta collected 88 boxes of leaflets from the printer, and each box held 7 leaflets. The hall where the campaign meets holds 300 people. At the station 141 leaflets were handed out on the first morning. Her colleague Dan, whose own stack had run out days earlier, noticed that every remaining leaflet carried 7 discount vouchers along its edge. All those vouchers were then shared equally among the 5 shops taking part, and Marta delivered the bundle for the bakery. How many vouchers did the bakery receive?

Marek had 65 bottle caps in his collecting tin. His friend Ines, whose tin was fuller than his, handed him 72 caps she no longer wanted. Marek then traded 75 caps away for a set of badges. The collectors club has 19 members. At the annual swap each cap he still owned was valued at 4 club points, and every club point could be exchanged for 8 raffle numbers. The organiser gave Marek 44 extra raffle numbers for helping to set up. How many raffle numbers did Marek hold?

Tara kept 28 seed potatoes in a paper sack over the winter. In March she planted 23 of them in her allotment beds. From each potato still in the sack she later grew a plant that produced 5 new potatoes, and she gathered those in. Her family ate 22 of the harvested potatoes over the following fortnight. Her neighbour Femi, who had grown far more than she had, gave her one potato for every potato she had left, doubling her store. Tara then bought 61 potatoes at the market and put them in the same sack. How many potatoes were in Tara's sack?

The station car park held 25 cars when the barrier was raised in the morning, and it charges by the minute rather than by the hour. In the first hour 17 more cars drove in. Before nine o'clock 33 cars left for the early train connections, and 4 more drove out shortly afterwards. Over the afternoon 78 cars arrived for the shopping centre. In the early evening 26 cars left, and 55 arrived for the concert at the arena. How many cars were in the car park at the end of the evening?

The swimming gala printed 150 programmes for the opening night, and the office found 24 more from the heats. Ticket demand meant the printer ran a second batch so that the pile became double its size. A club official then brought 20 programmes from the reception desk. For the regional tour the organisers ordered triple that pile, having 3 copies made of every programme. A cupboard search turned up 41 programmes from last season, which were added to the boxes, and race times are written in seconds rather than in minutes. How many programmes were in the boxes?

The charity shop had 181 second-hand books on its shelves at the start of the week. Donations brought in 75 more books on the Tuesday. A dozen volunteers take turns behind the till. A clearance sale on the Saturday sold 255 books to a dealer who arrived with a van. The manager sent whatever was left to a printer, who produced 7 copies of it for the hospital reading group. Of those copies, 4 were given away at the first meeting. How many copies did the reading group still have?

The market stall opened the morning with 73 wicker baskets on the trestle. Before eleven o'clock 26 baskets had been sold to café owners. The stallholder then found that every basket still on the trestle held 4 ripe pears. During the afternoon 142 pears were sold loose to passing shoppers. In the early evening the orchard van delivered 32 more pears to the stall, and a neighbouring grower handed over 38 pears he could not sell. How many pears were on the stall at the end of the day?

The candle workshop opened the morning with 6 crates on the bench, and every crate held 36 candles. By midday 130 candles had been sold to the gift shop in town. During the afternoon the chandler poured and finished 19 new candles, which joined the others on the bench. In the evening every candle was boxed with 2 long matches for the winter market. The packer added 16 spare matches to the box of supplies. How many matches were used or set aside in total?

The juice bar started the day with 172 oranges in its crate. Each orange was cut into 3 wedges for the press, so the count of pieces tripled. A member of staff found 3 wedges left over from the day before and put them with the rest. The bar has 14 stools along its counter. The morning rush used 106 wedges, and the afternoon got through 390 more. A late delivery was cut up to give 34 extra wedges. How many wedges did the bar have at the end?

Kofi began the mosaic project with 79 ceramic tiles. His sister Amara, whose box held more than his, gave him 70 tiles from her own supply. Every tile was then scored and snapped into 4 small squares. Amara handed over 59 loose squares she had already cut, and Kofi found 52 more squares in a tin under the bench. The competition itself ran for 6 hours. Each square placed in the mosaic is worth 9 points from the judges. How many points was Kofi's mosaic worth?

The allotment shed held 193 onion sets at the start of the planting weekend. Jonas planted 99 of them in the long bed by the fence. He put another 51 into the raised bed near the shed. Frost got into the shed and spoiled 30 of the sets that were still there. His neighbour Rita, who had bought far more than Jonas, gave him 72 sets from her own tray. Every set that went into the ground produced 2 onions at harvest. How many onions were harvested from those sets?

The hospital shop had 98 newspapers on its stand when it opened in the morning. The delivery driver brought in 17 more before eight o'clock, and a second drop added 14. The ward upstairs has 30 beds. During the afternoon a wholesaler left 44 newspapers at the door, and in the early evening a dozen volunteers helped carry in 19 more from the van. Customers bought 61 newspapers over the course of the day. How many newspapers were left on the stand?

The leisure centre had 182 lockers standing empty when it opened in the morning. A cleaner cleared out 28 more that had been left locked overnight. Early swimmers took 31 of the free lockers before nine o'clock. At midday a school group filled 129 lockers in one noisy rush. In the evening 10 more lockers were taken by the badminton club. How many lockers were still empty at the end of the day?

A dairy had 117 wheels of cheese maturing on its racks. It sold 55 of them to a wholesaler in the spring. A restaurant chain took another 26 wheels in the same month. Every wheel still on the racks was later cut into 7 wedges for the farm shop. The cheesemaker added 30 wedges from an older batch in the cold store and 25 wedges that had come back from a market stall. Each wedge is wrapped in 2 sheets of waxed paper before it goes on sale. How many sheets of waxed paper were needed?

The warden counted 140 geese on the lake at first light. Another 47 dropped onto the water during the early morning, and 72 more came in from the fields before noon. Around midday 39 of the geese flew off towards the estuary. During the afternoon a further 50 geese landed on the far side of the lake. In the evening 47 more arrived as the light went. How many geese were on the lake at dusk?

The florist opened the morning with 168 stems in her buckets, and a dozen buckets stand along the back wall. A grower delivered 22 more stems before the shop got busy. Customers bought 62 stems during the morning. The florist then wired 4 silk leaves onto every stem that was still in the shop. During the afternoon 32 spare leaves arrived in a craft order, and in the evening a wholesaler sent 65 more. How many silk leaves did the florist have?

Hina spent the morning packing 146 gift boxes, and each box was filled with 7 scented candles. Every candle was then wrapped in 4 sheets of tissue paper before the lid went on. The drive to the northern shops takes 3 hours. During the afternoon the tissue-wrapped candles were shared equally among 4 delivery vans, and Hina's colleague Sam drove the van bound for Leeds. In the evening Sam was given 21 extra sheets of tissue for repacking on the road. How many sheets of tissue paper were in Sam's van?

A mail-order company sent out 43 parcels of books in the first week, and 1 of them was lost by the carrier and written off. The following week it despatched 61 more parcels. The delivery van covers 90 kilometres on its round. Every parcel that arrived safely contained 5 books, and half of the titles were paperbacks. The warehouse then added 65 single books that had been ordered without a parcel. Each book on the invoice is priced at 8 dollars, and the invoice is written in dollars rather than in cents. What is the total price in dollars?

The seed shop opened the morning with 123 seed trays on its outdoor bench. A landscaper arrived early and bought 115 of them for a park contract. Every tray still on the bench was found to hold 5 small pots. During the afternoon the owner counted 9 bulbs planted in each of those pots. She then added 67 loose bulbs from a sack in the shed. In the evening she calculated that every bulb would open 3 flowers next spring. How many flowers should the bulbs produce?

A hardware shop had 178 padlocks hanging on its display wall, and it sells chain by the centimetre rather than by the metre. Customers bought 21 padlocks in the first week of the sale. A wholesaler then delivered 55 more. Over the second week 66 padlocks were sold to a storage firm. A late order brought in 73 further padlocks. Every padlock on the wall carries 9 loyalty stamps for the customer who buys it. How many loyalty stamps are on the display wall?

Ola designed 76 posters for the museum campaign, and her colleague Tomas, who had made far fewer, gave her the 5 he had drawn. Every poster in the set was printed in 3 languages for the different districts. Each language version was then copied for all 8 branches of the museum service. Print sizes on the order are given in millimetres rather than in centimetres. Each branch copy has to be franked with 4 postage stamps to reach its site. How many postage stamps are needed?

In the morning 4 lorries pulled into the grain yard, and each lorry carried 234 sacks. Half of the lorries in the fleet are less than a year old. Before noon 894 sacks were delivered on to the mill down the road. During the afternoon every sack still in the yard was split into 8 smaller bags for the retail trade. In the evening the storeman brought out 45 more bags that had been made up the previous week. How many bags were in the yard?
